wolfram-debugging.notes: Who is right about 'an Assert is skipped after a call with Assert off': the run is right, for the condition it stated (Assert stays Off; the 'Assertions' handler, hence FailedAssertions, then sees nothing on later calls). Reproduced in my fresh kernels and visible in the run's own saved notebook (Count 0 before re-Get, 1 after). The orchestrator's script does not test that condition: every case turns On[Assert] before the second call, and toggling On/Off (even On then Off) resets the effect (my case 5), so its result does not contradict the claim. Refinements the run did not establish: it affects Block-scoped bodies only in my tests (Module and unscoped bodies are not affected); ClearSystemCache does not reset it, re-Get / redefinition or an On/Off toggle does. The run's Trace evidence is not discriminating: in Mathematica 15 Trace of Compute[1] with Assert Off shows no separate Assert step even on the very first call, before any plain call (scratch-G/assert2.wls: the Assert appears only inside the Block/CompoundExpression entries; the run's own fresh3 output also printed {} for 'Trace fresh Compute[1]' right after Get), so 'Trace shows no Assert step' should be dropped from the claim. This is a real false-negative trap in the skill's recommended helper (its usage says it works 'also when Assert is Off') and should be recorded in tests/bugs/BUGS.md and the skill adaptation: call FailedAssertions right after (re)loading the definitions, before any plain call.
